What is evidence, and what is an assumption?

This is a mechanism-testing educational sandbox, not a calibrated reconstruction of Angkor. The reference preset is an evidence-oriented starting point, not an estimated historical parameter vector. In particular, workforce share, captive supply, conflict probabilities, corvée days and maintenance coefficients are hypothetical.

Model structure

140 landscape cells, with arable area, population, fertility, irrigation condition and court loyalty. Annual rain shocks affect yield and maintenance; simulated households aggregate into cohorts. Court revenue finances armies and architecture; rival pressure causes endogenous raids, victories, defeats and occasional sacks. Labor includes corvée, bonded workers and seasonal religious mobility. Temple activity and court legitimacy evolve separately. This is a spatial cohort model, not a fully individual household ABM.

A fixed agricultural demand is assumed at 200 kg unmilled rice equivalent per resident annually, and food trade is simplified. Monument output is a log of cumulative ornamental worker-days, not cubic meters of sandstone. Military units represent seasonal soldiers, not actual excavated troop counts. Population density uses the full region, not the ceremonial core.

Sources to review before calibration

Klassen, Evans and Fletcher, work on Angkor's agricultural landscapes and water infrastructure; Carter et al., 2021 Angkor population reconstruction; Lustig & Lustig on Angkorian temple labor; Zhou Daguan, Customs of Cambodia; Lucero, Fletcher & Coningham on low-density tropical urbanism; Stephen Lansing on Balinese water temples. See MODEL_CARD.md in this ZIP for research tasks and falsification tests.

How to hand this to an AI coding assistant

Unzip the folder and ask an assistant to open index.html, read model.js and MODEL_CARD.md, then change or extend parameters while preserving seeded reproducibility and the tests. It runs without internet or dependencies. Charts are native Canvas and the engine is standalone JavaScript.
